waveName: Wave 6 – Deviation map & batch editing, real fine tiles, colour measuring, streaming CSV, final PDF wiring

package.title: Streaming CSV for millions of stones and paper-matched section presets
package.goal: 'Alle Koordinaten als CSV' works at 5M stones without freezing or failing silently, and includes template numbers and correct colour names. Section sizes can match the paper with one click.
steps: csv.ts: add buildCsvChunks(...) as a Generator<string> yielding a header and then bands of about 20k rows. Keep buildCsv as a join of the chunks. Columns use paletteDisplayName and write the Zuschnitt value as 'ja (T12)' using the collectTemplates numbering. Section exports iterate the section's own range instead of filtering the whole grid. Throw a translated error if maxColorIndex ≥ palette.length.
csv.worker.ts plus a new client channel 'csv': fold the chunks into a Blob every 32 MB, post progress, and finally post {blob, rows}. No string copy on the main thread.

StepPlan exportCsv: show progress and an Abbrechen button. Prepend the BOM. Pass the result to downloadBlob and show SaveResultNote. When there are more than 1,048,576 rows, warn that Excel and LibreOffice cannot open that many.

StepPlan section settings: add presets '1 Blatt' and '2×2 Blätter', set from printableArea(rec.pdfOptions)/sheetScale. Add a hint when the current sections leave thin strips (using planSheets). Ask for confirmation if laying progress exists, because section IDs change.
acceptance: Unit tests: on the portrait and city samples, the joined chunks are byte-identical to the old buildCsv output, apart from the intended T# and name changes, which are listed. Data rows equal stats pieces, and Position values are unique.
Node test: a synthetic mosaic of about 3.5M cells streams without a RangeError; sum the chunk lengths instead of joining them.
e2e: at 2M stones there is no main-thread long task over 100 ms during export, and the file arrives.
package.risk: Effort M. Android writes rely on the chunked saving from wave 2. The per-section ZIP is deferred.

findings.title: 'Alle Koordinaten als CSV' fails silently at 5M stones and freezes the UI at 2M
findings.problem: buildCsv builds the entire CSV as one JS string (csv.ts:26 to 66, out.join). At about 5M stones this exceeds V8's maximum string length and the worker throws 'Invalid string length'. exportCsv in StepPlan.tsx (lines 35 to 50) has try/finally without catch, so the user sees the button return to normal and nothing else. No error and no file. The PDF itself tells users that 'the complete list is available as CSV export' (pdf.coordsTruncated), so huge projects have no complete coordinate list at all. At 2M the string is about 350 MB. It is copied through postMessage to the main thread and then into a Blob, which blocks the UI for seconds and peaks around 1 GB.
findings.evidence: Node, synthetic mosaic with 10 % diagonal cells (bench-csv.ts): 2,003,001 cells takes 9.9 s and produces a 354 MB string, peak RSS 994 MB. 5,004,501 cells gives {"error":"RangeError: Invalid string length","ms":24480}. Browser 2M (1000x500 cm, 4 mm): 330 MB download in 10.0 s, worker 6.9 s, one main-thread long task of 2,318 ms (.../performance-scale/browser-csv2m.log). Browser 5M (1250x1000 cm, 4 mm): the worker fails after 15.8 s, console shows 'Error: Invalid string length', no element with class error is shown, button text is back to 'Alle Koordinaten als CSV', and no download arrives within 180 s (.../performance-scale/browser-csv5m.log, screenshot browser/csv5m/after-csv.png). All paths are under /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-MosaicPlan/2af1e5b3-d1bd-540e-aeb5-6edf8b6b0ca5/scratchpad/audit/performance-scale/.
findings.proposal: Stream the CSV instead of building one string. In the worker, generate chunks per band of 64 rows (or per section), encode each with TextEncoder and post it as a transferable ArrayBuffer with progress. On the main thread, collect the chunks and call new Blob(chunks) once; Blob parts never form a single JS string. On Android, append the chunks with Filesystem.appendFile. For a very large export, also offer one CSV per section in a ZIP (store-only ZIP is about 60 lines). Shrink rows by about 2x: leave out 'Kontur_mm' for uncut axis-aligned rectangles (it is exactly X/Y/Breite/Hoehe) and print it only for cut pieces. Move Farbname/HEX to a small legend CSV. Add catch to exportCsv and show the error.

findings.title: Cut pieces on the laying sheets don't point to their cut template, and tiny pieces carry no colour code
findings.problem: drawSheet() prints only the 2-digit colour code on every piece (pdf.ts:579-598). Pieces whose bounding box is under 1.8 mm on paper get no label at all (pdf.ts:592). The only links from a piece to its template are (a) the template box, which lists at most 12 IDs (collectTemplates, pdf.ts:69), and (b) the coordinate list, which stops at coordLimit (default 20 000). So at the wall, the user sees a trapezoid or sliver on the sheet and cannot find out which template (T#) to cut it from. This is the central requirement-5/9 link between the laying plan and the cut templates.
findings.evidence: Repro /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-MosaicPlan/2af1e5b3-d1bd-540e-aeb5-6edf8b6b0ca5/scratchpad/audit/pdf-print/orphan.ts (200x100 cm, 8 mm, default PDF options) prints: "cutPieces=1914 cut pieces without any template reference in the PDF=753" (39 %). persize.ts: on the template boxes alone, 50 % (2x1 m), 24 % (30x40 cm/5 mm) and 57 % (60x40 cm/12 mm) of cut-piece IDs are not listed. The text in the content streams of the laying-sheet pages 9/10/12/13 of out/a4p_5mm_1to1.pdf contains 0 strings of the form 'T<n>'. codes.py: page 9 has 1059 stones drawn but only about 1035 code labels, so the missing ones are the small cut slivers. Visual: png/a5hi-09-eye.png (eye area: slivers with no code, trapezoids with no T#).
findings.proposal: In drawSheet, for non-FULL cells get ci = pieceCutInfo(cache, …) (the cache and tpl = collectTemplates(...) already exist before the sheet loop, pdf.ts:421) and tg = tpl.bySig.get(ci.signature). If the piece's inscribed size on paper is at least 3.5 mm, print two lines: the code and a small 'T12'. If it is smaller, draw a numbered callout dot (①②…) at the centroid and add a 'Zuschnitte auf diesem Blatt' table in the sheet's bottom reserve (marker · ID · code · T# · outer size). Add printH reserve for it, or continue on a follow-up page labelled with the sheet ID. On each template, replace the 12-ID list with occurrences per sheet ('A1-1: 14×, A1-2: 3×') so every instance can be traced. Use the same signature mapping the coordinate list uses, so no new geometry is invented. Add a vitest check: every cut piece's T# appears either on its sheet or in that sheet's table.
corrected:
All changes go in src/core/pdf.ts (plus src/core/csv.ts and tests). Every T# comes from the existing tpl.bySig signature mapping, so no new geometry is computed.

1. Print T# on the sheet.
   - In drawSheet, for each non-FULL piece: ci = pieceCutInfo(cache, layout, data, row, col, i, p.poly, raw(p.color)).
   - If ci.needsCut, look up tg = tpl.bySig.get(ci.signature). tpl, cache and raw already exist before the sheet loop.
   - Mark the template as printed only if opts.includeTemplates is true and tg.no <= opts.templateLimit.
   - If min(bbox)*s is at least about 3.5 mm and a T# font of at least 3 pt fits, print the code plus a second small line: 'T12' if printed, otherwise a scissors-free marker such as '*'.

2. Callouts for small pieces.
   - Cover cut pieces that are too small for two lines, and every piece that currently gets no code (the line 592 rule).
   - Draw a small circle (doc.circle) at the centroid with a plain running number 1..n per sheet, in helvetica digits. Do not use Unicode circled digits.

3. Cut list page per sheet.
   - When a sheet has any cut pieces, add a 'Zuschnittliste Blatt A1-3' page right after it. Do not shrink printH or bottomReserve.
   - Use the existing table() helper with columns: No. | Position ID (cellId + -i) | colour code + swatch | T# (or 'Vorlage nicht gedruckt') | shape | outer size w x h mm.

4. Template boxes.
   - In collectTemplates, also count occurrences per sheet.
   - Print 'A1-1: 14x, A1-2: 3x ...' instead of the first 12 IDs.

5. CSV.
   - In csv.ts, write the Zuschnitt column as 'ja (T12)', using the same collectTemplates numbering.

6. Vitest.
   - For a sample project, check that every cut piece on each generated sheet has either an on-piece T# or a cut-list row.
   - Check that no referenced T# is greater than templateLimit.
   - Check that every piece is labelled with its colour code either on the sheet or in the list.

src/core/pdf.ts:
(1) Add a pure exported function sheetCutList(layout, data, palette, materials, tpl, cache, r0, r1, c0, c1, s, showCodes). It returns one entry {id, code, shape, tNo|null, w, h} for every needsCut piece and for every piece whose code label was suppressed. Sort by row, then column. It reuses pieceCutInfo, tpl.bySig and pieceId, so no new geometry. In drawSheet, when the list is non-empty, print it on a follow-up page titled 'Zuschnittliste Blatt A1-3' (same header, page numbering included), in 4-5 compact columns of about 4 mm rows: 'C014-2 · 07 · Trapez · T12 · 7,9×4,1'. Continue on more pages labelled with the same sheet ID; at most about 200 entries per A4 page. This list is not subject to coordLimit.
(2) On the sheet, print the T# as a small second line inside the piece only when 4*area/perimeter*s >= ~4.5 mm (helps at 8-12 mm tiles or 2:1). No callout dots.
(3) Mark each piece whose code is suppressed with a tiny hollow dot (meaning 'see the cut list'), so slivers are never silently unlabelled. Only computed codes are shown.
(4) Never print a bare T# for a template that is not in the PDF. Keep global numbering so separately printed sections stay consistent. When opts.sectionIds is set, always print the templates referenced by the selected sections. If includeTemplates is false or tNo > templateLimit, print 'T512 (nicht im PDF)'. Apply the same rule to the coordinate list at pdf.ts:842.
(5) In drawTemplate, replace the 12-ID list with occurrences per sheet ('A1-3: 14×, A2-1: 3×' ...), built in collectTemplates by also recording the sheet. Truncate with '…' when the box is full.
(6) Vitest in tests/pdf.test.ts: for 2-3 sample projects, every cut piece in the selected sections appears exactly once, in sheetCutList for the sheet containing its cell. Its tNo equals tpl.bySig.get(signature).no. The sum of cut entries equals computeStats(...).cutPieces for those sections. The test also checks the i18n keys in de/en/tr. If showCodes is false for a whole sheet (e.g. 2 mm tiles at 1:1), print a warning on the sheet to choose scale >= 2:1 instead of listing every stone.

findings.title: Auto colour names are wrong and duplicated in the legend and PDF (pure red = 'Orange', 8× 'Blassblau')
findings.problem: describeColor() applies HSV-style hue cut-offs to CIELAB hue angles. sRGB red has h_ab of about 40°, so every red is named Orange, Dunkelorange or Dunkelbraun; blue becomes 'Dunkelviolett' and yellow 'Hellgelbgrün'. Names are also not unique: the portrait legend has 8× Blassblau, 7× Dunkelbraun and 4× Hellbeige, and the red sweater is listed as 'Dunkelbraun'. These names go into the legend, the palette table and the PDF that the user shops and lays from.
findings.evidence: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-MosaicPlan/2af1e5b3-d1bd-540e-aeb5-6edf8b6b0ca5/scratchpad/audit/ux-desktop/ts/names.out: '#FF0000 h=40.0 -> Orange', '#C00000 -> Orange', '#800000 -> Dunkelorange', '#841929 -> Dunkelbraun', '#0000FF -> Dunkelviolett', '#FFFF00 -> Hellgelbgrün'. Legend: shots/j2-09-colors-after-compute.png (codes 06-20 = Blassblau ×8, 25/27-32 = Dunkelbraun ×7). PDF: `pdftotext portrait.pdf | grep -c Blassblau` = 29. Code: src/core/color.ts describeColor() (the 'if (h < 20 || h >= 345) base = red' chain).
findings.proposal: Replace the hue chain with nearest-reference naming. Keep a curated table of about 40 named reference colours per language (German: Rot, Karminrot, Weinrot, Rosa, Lachs, Terrakotta, Orange, Ocker, Gelb, Oliv, Grün, Türkis, Hellblau, Blau, Marine, Violett, Braun, Beige, Haut hell/mittel/dunkel, Grau …) stored as Lab, and pick the name by minimum ΔE2000. Then make names unique inside a palette: when several entries share a name, append a lightness rank by L* ('Blassblau hell / mittel / dunkel', then '… 1/2/3'). Store PaletteColor.autoName=true so auto names are regenerated on language switch (today Turkish names stay after switching back to DE, see journey3 output), while user-edited names are kept.
corrected:
1) In src/core/color.ts, replace the hue chain in `describeColor` with a lookup of the nearest reference colour.
- Add a constant `COLOR_REFS: { key: string; lab: Lab }[]` with about 40-50 language-neutral keys: white, cream, lightgray, gray, darkgray, black, red, lightred, darkred, wine, carmine, pink, oldrose, salmon, orange, lightorange, terracotta, ochre, yellow, lightyellow, mustard, olive, yellowgreen, lightgreen, green, darkgreen, turquoise, petrol, lightblue, skyblue, blue, greyblue, darkblue, navy, violet, lilac, aubergine, magenta, plum, brown, darkbrown, lightbrown, beige, sand, skin_light, skin_medium, skin_dark.
- Each key holds the Lab of a typical sRGB sample, for example red=#D01818, blue=#2050C0, yellow=#F8E020, carmine=#A01830, skin_medium=#D8A07C.
- Translate each key per language in the existing NAMES table for de/en/tr.
- Export `colorNameKey(lab)`, which returns the key with the minimum `deltaE2000`, and keep `describeColor(lab, lang) = NAMES[lang][colorNameKey(lab)]`.
- Prototype that confirms the approach: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-MosaicPlan/2af1e5b3-d1bd-540e-aeb5-6edf8b6b0ca5/scratchpad/audit/verify-ux-desktop-3/proto.ts

2) Make names unique within a palette.
- Add a helper `nameAutoPalette(palette, lang)` in src/core/edits.ts.
- Call it at the end of `computeMosaic` (mosaic.ts around line 573) and after `addPaletteColor` and `updatePaletteColor`.
- It groups auto-named entries by key, sorts each group from lightest to darkest L*, and appends a plain number ('Blau 1', 'Blau 2', …) only when a key appears more than once.
- Do not use hell/mittel/dunkel as the suffix, because many names already contain Hell or Dunkel.

3) Keep names right when the language changes, without rewriting user names.
- Add the optional fields `nameKey?: string` and `nameIdx?: number` to `PaletteColor` in src/core/types.ts. Set them only for auto names. Persist them in src/core/serialize.ts and IndexedDB, and carry them through `FixedColor` for custom palette mode (useProject.ts:295).
- `updatePaletteColor` with an explicit `name`, and adopting a material's colorName (StepColors.tsx:122), must clear `nameKey`.
- Add a selector `displayName(p, lang)` that returns `NAMES[lang][p.nameKey] + (p.nameIdx ? ' ' + p.nameIdx : '')` when `nameKey` is set and `p.name` otherwise.
- Use `displayName` in StepPreview, StepColors, StoneDialog, pdf.ts:328/521 (pass `locale`) and csv.ts:54.
- Projects saved before this change have no `nameKey`, so they keep their stored names, which is safe.

4) Tests in tests/core.test.ts:
- `describeColor(hexToLab('#FF0000'), 'de')` is 'Rot'; '#0000FF' gives 'Blau'; '#FFFF00' gives 'Gelb'; '#8B4513' contains 'braun'.
- The palette from the portrait pipeline has unique display names in de, en and tr.
- After changing language, auto names change and a user-edited name stays the same.

Impact 3-4, effort S-M.

1. **Rewrite describeColor().** In src/core/color.ts, keep one table of about 50 reference colours. Each entry has a Lab value and a name in de, en and tr. Do not keep separate tables per language.
   - Include common tile and portrait colours: Rot, Dunkelrot (#8B0000), Karminrot, Weinrot, Bordeaux, Rosa, Altrosa, Pink, Magenta, Lachs, Apricot, Terrakotta, Rostbraun, Orange (#FFA500 and #F08000), Ocker, Senfgelb, Gelb, Hellgelb, Oliv, Gelbgrün, Hellgrün, Grün, Dunkelgrün, Salbeigrün, Türkis, Petrol, Hellblau, Himmelblau, Blau, Taubenblau, Graublau, Stahlblau/dunkles Graublau (#3C5670), Marineblau, Violett, Flieder, Aubergine, Hellbraun, Braun, Dunkelbraun, Beige, Sand, Creme, Haut hell/mittel/dunkel.
   - Keep the existing grey branch first: if chroma C* < ~6, name the colour Weiß/Hellgrau/Grau/Dunkelgrau/Schwarz by L* alone.
   - Otherwise pick the reference with the smallest ΔE2000.
   - If that smallest ΔE is above ~8 and |ΔL*| is above 12, add "Hell"/"Dunkel" in front, using the existing prefix and lowercasing rules.

2. **Pin the names with tests in tests/core.test.ts, for all three languages.**
   - #FF0000→Rot, #800000→Dunkelrot, #841929→Weinrot, #FFA500→Orange, #FFFF00→Gelb, #0000FF→Blau, #008000→Grün, #DFA382→Haut*, #8B4513→Braun.
   - The existing white, black and #9fc5f8 checks.
   - Use the portrait palette hexes from j2-09 as further cases.
   - For a starting point see /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-MosaicPlan/2af1e5b3-d1bd-540e-aeb5-6edf8b6b0ca5/scratchpad/audit/value-ux-desktop-3/proto.ts and proto.out in the same folder.

3. **Track which names are automatic.** Add an optional `autoName?: boolean` to PaletteColor in src/core/types.ts.
   - Set it to true wherever describeColor supplies the name: mosaic.ts:579 and edits.ts:155.
   - Carry it through the fixed-palette data at mosaic.ts:462 and 468, so a recompute keeps it.
   - Set it to false when the user types a name (StepColors.tsx:193) or adopts a material colour name (StepColors.tsx:122).
   - When the colours are recomputed, the UI language changes, or a PDF is exported, regenerate only names where autoName is true.
   - Saved projects without the flag: mark a name as automatic only if it equals legacyDescribeColor(lab, de|en|tr). Keep the current function under that name just for this check. Otherwise keep the name as it is.

4. **Optionally, make repeated names easier to tell apart.** Do this only for automatic names, and only when the same name appears more than once in a palette.
   - Add a qualifier based on lightness order within that group: (hell/dunkel) for 2, (hell/mittel/dunkel) for 3, and "sehr hell … sehr dunkel" for up to 5.
   - Never add numbers, because they would clash with the two-digit colour code.
   - Beyond 5, let the name repeat; the colour code stays the unique identifier.
   - Keep names to about 22 characters or less so the PDF legend column still fits.

This changes only the labels. Codes, counts, Lab and HEX values, and geometry are untouched, and no code looks anything up by colour name.

findings.title: 'Palette aus Materialien' after a compute swaps the palette without remapping stones, so the whole mosaic changes colours (black face)
findings.problem: In custom-palette mode, the 'Palette aus Materialien' button calls api.setPalette() with a freshly built array in material order. The computed mosaic stores palette indices, and compute had already re-sorted the palette by lightness. Every stone therefore silently gets another colour: the face becomes black and the hair light blue. The preview, the stats and the PDF all use the scrambled mapping. Only the generic stale badge appears. Other paths that change palette length or order without remapping can produce indices ≥ palette.length.
findings.evidence: Repro: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-MosaicPlan/2af1e5b3-d1bd-540e-aeb5-6edf8b6b0ca5/scratchpad/audit/correctness-ui-state/t12_palette_replace_after_compute.cjs, output t12_output.txt. Before: '02 Haut hell 300 | 03 Hellblau 1.176 | ... | 10 Schwarz 215'. After: '02 Schwarz 300 | 03 Haut hell 1.176 | ... | 10 Grau 215 | 11 Gruen 0 | 12 Rosa 0'. Same stone counts, different colours. Side-by-side t12-before-after.png in the same folder. Code: StepColors.tsx:144-155 (setPalette(p) with no remap, even when api.computed exists); compare removePaletteColor in edits.ts:174-193, which does remap.
findings.proposal: Add a remapPalette(oldPalette, newPalette, data, formula) helper to edits.ts. It maps each old index to its new index by materialId, then exact hex, then nearest ΔE, and rewrites c1/c2/sub/free via remapAll. Call it from every palette-replacing action when api.computed is set ('Palette aus Materialien', and any future import), followed by touchMosaic(). Otherwise disable the button after compute, with the hint 'Erst neu berechnen'. Add an invariant check (max index < palette.length) in the loader and before PDF/CSV generation, and show an error instead of printing wrong colours.
corrected:
The direction is right. Here it is made precise:

(1) In src/core/edits.ts, add `export function remapToPalette(oldP: PaletteColor[], newP: PaletteColor[], data: MosaicData, formula): void`.
- Build a lookup `map[old] -> new` for each old index: same materialId first, then the same hex (case-insensitive), then the nearest new colour by ΔE (NearestColorMatcher over newP.lab).
- Apply it with the existing remapAll. Export remapAll or call it internally.

(2) In StepColors.tsx, change the 'Palette aus Materialien' onClick:
- When api.computed is set, call remapToPalette(palette, p, api.computed.data, rec.settings.deltaE), then api.setPalette(p), then api.touchMosaic(). This is the same order remove() already uses at lines 111-114.
- Keep the stale state, since cp changes, so the user is still asked to recompute. Ask for confirmation first, e.g. 'Mosaik wird auf die neue Palette umgefärbt (nächste Farbe) – für ein optimales Ergebnis neu berechnen'.
- The simpler alternative is to hide or disable this button while api.computed exists and show 'Erst neu berechnen'.

(3) Add an invariant so wrong results can never be printed silently:
- In src/core/stats.ts:172-173, count stones whose index is out of range in an `invalidColorPieces` counter instead of skipping them with `continue`.
- In StepPdf.tsx, StepPlan.tsx and the CSV export, refuse to generate output and show an error ('Farbzuordnung ungültig – bitte neu berechnen') when that counter is above 0, or when a max-index scan of c1/c2/sub/free is ≥ palette.length.
- When useProject.ts loads a mosaic, run the same scan. If it fails, mark the project as needing a recompute instead of rendering magenta stones.

(4) Add a vitest that computes in custom mode, replaces the palette in another order with fewer entries, applies the remap, and then checks two things: every index is below palette.length, and the stats piece total still equals the total from geometry.

1) StepColors.tsx:144-152, the 'Palette aus Materialien' button. When api.computed is null, keep today's replace behaviour. When api.computed exists, MERGE so that existing indices and codes stay stable:
   a) For each material with a valid hex that is not yet in the palette (match by materialId, then by exact upper-case hex), append it with addPaletteColor(..., m.id). Appending never invalidates an index.
   b) Find the palette entries that have no material counterpart, i.e. no materialId among the current materials and no exact hex match. Remove them in DESCENDING index order with the existing removePaletteColor(palette, api.computed.data, i, undefined, rec.settings.deltaE), which already moves their stones to the nearest remaining colour by ΔE. Before applying, count the affected stones from api.stats.perColor and show a confirm dialog such as 'N Steine werden auf die nächste Materialfarbe umgestellt (max. ΔE x) – fortfahren?'. Afterwards show the same numbers as a notice.
   c) Call api.setPalette(next) and then api.touchMosaic(). Leave the stale badge on, because a recompute could make use of the newly added colours.
   If you want a single helper, put mergePaletteFromMaterials(palette, data, materials, formula) in edits.ts. It returns {palette, movedStones, maxDeltaE} and is built from addPaletteColor and removePaletteColor. Do not build a full reorder remap, since that renumbers codes and makes printed sheets wrong.
2) Invariant guard. Add assertPaletteIndices(data, palette) to src/core/edits.ts (or types.ts). It scans c1/c2 (only where kind uses them), sub and free, and returns the maximum index. Call it:
   - in useProject's loader after unpackMosaic;
   - in the stats worker;
   - at the start of buildPdf and buildCsv.
   On a violation, do not print magenta stones or undercounted totals. Show a clear error ('Farbzuordnung beschädigt – bitte neu berechnen'), block PDF/CSV export and offer a recompute.
3) Tests in tests/core.test.ts:
   - Compute in custom mode from 12 materials, run the merge, and assert that every piece keeps its hex, total pieces are unchanged and all indices are < palette.length.
   - Run the merge with a shrunk material list and assert that the moved-stone count equals the stones of the removed colours and that the total is unchanged.
   - buildCsv and buildPdf throw on out-of-range indices.
   Reproduction of the current failure modes: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-MosaicPlan/2af1e5b3-d1bd-540e-aeb5-6edf8b6b0ca5/scratchpad/audit/value-correctness-ui-state-3/remap_check.ts.

findings.title: Sheet splitting wastes about half the paper: thin leftover strips, oversized margins, one full page per section cover
findings.problem: The default section size (300×300 mm) does not relate to the paper's printable area (A4 portrait 1:1: 178×247 mm). tilesOf() splits greedily (pdf.ts:433-446), so many sections become one full sheet plus a 16–40 mm strip on a separate page. Fixed reserves (M=10, top 19, bottom 21, pdf.ts:84/427-429) take 60 of 297 mm. Every section also gets a separate cover page that is mostly empty. The UI estimate (StepPdf.tsx:31-36: PH-53 and ceil(w/printW)) uses different numbers from pdf.ts (PH-50 and grid-aligned greedy split).

Smaller margins are low priority: they help only by coincidence and need a relayout of the T-9 column labels, the ruler, and the PH-M-9 side info line. 1:1 scale, grid-aligned sheet edges and the joining marks must stay unchanged; add a test that sheets × printable area ≥ section area and that the PDF page count equals the UI estimate.

**1. (S, do first) Balanced sheet split.**
- Export a balancedSplit(pos, size, a, b, maxLen) from layout.ts. It is the existing splitAxis logic, generalized to a sub-range.
- Use it in computeSections and in pdf.ts tilesOf, with maxLen = printW/s and printH/s.
- This removes every narrow strip (e.g. A1-2 at X 171-197 mm becomes two sheets of about 98 mm) without changing sheet count, section IDs or geometry.
- The mini sheet overview, join labels and registration crosses all come from cx/ry, so they stay consistent.
- Keep the PDF==preview per-colour count test and add one: for every section, no sheet is narrower than 40% of the printable width unless the section itself is.

**2. (M) One source of truth for the printable area.**
- Add printableArea(opts) and SHEET_RESERVES {M:10, top:19, left:12, bottom:21} to pdfOptions.ts.
- Use them in pdf.ts:427-431 and in StepPdf's estimate.
- Have StepPdf compute the estimate with the same grid-aligned split instead of ceil(w/printW).

**3. (M) Paper-aligned sections.**
- Add sectionMode 'sheets' with sheetsPerSection X/Y, default 2x2.
- Compute sheet boundaries for the whole project first:
  - Walk the real colX/colW and rowY/rowH greedily against printW/sheetScale and printH/sheetScale, so cut edge cells and different tile sizes are handled exactly.
  - Rebalance these boundaries over the whole project.
- Group k x k sheets into one section, so section edges always fall on sheet edges.
- In this mode tilesOf returns exactly those global boundaries.
- Expected results: 2000x1000 cm drops from 126 to about 90 pages, 10000x5000 from 2890 to about 1570, with no strips.
- Make it the default only for NEW projects.
- In the PDF step, show a hint when paper use is under about 70% or strips exist, for example: "Abschnitte passen schlecht zu A4: 12 Blätter, 6 davon schmal – Abschnitte an Papier anpassen (8 Blätter)".
- Ask for confirmation if laying progress exists or a PDF was already exported, because section IDs and earlier printouts change. Progress is per cell, so no data is lost.
- Recompute when the paper format, orientation or scale changes.

**4. Orientation.**
- Do NOT mix orientations inside one PDF: print dialogs may auto-rotate or shrink to fit and break 1:1.
- Instead, let the estimate compute portrait vs landscape for the whole document and show "Querformat: N Blätter".

**5. Margins.**
- Keep M=10 so the calibration bar and labels survive printer non-printable edges.
- Only optional and verified by rendering: shrink bottomReserve by putting the joint hint and the calibration bar on one row.
- Only shrink topReserve if the sheet title moves into the running header first, because column labels at T-9 (pdf.ts:604) otherwise collide with the title at M+3.5 (pdf.ts:551).

**6. Section covers.**
- With k x k sections the cover overhead is already about 20%.
- Optionally, when exporting all sections, let covers flow: start a new page only when the next cover block (key data + legend table) does not fit in the space left. When printing a single section, keep its own cover page so it can still be printed separately.

globalRules:
Implementation plan for making MosaicPlan "much, much better": 7 waves, 33 work packages, ordered by user impact. The order is: (1) data safety and geometric correctness; (2) workspace safety UI, Android platform, honest colours, honest preview, photo intake and design system; (3) mosaic colour quality, live preview, freeform editor, face/detail guidance, viewer features, PDF foundations and project portability; (4) cut placement and accent colours, laying workbench, progress engine, PDF sheet structure, offline face detector; (5) undo/redo, single-pass stats, viewer back-buffer, PDF content, shopping view, target colours, PDF export UI; (6) deviation map and batch editing, fine-tile materials, colour measuring, streaming CSV, final PDF wiring; (7) docs and e2e consolidation.

RULES FOR EVERY PACKAGE

Files and parallel work
- Packages in the same wave run in parallel. They own disjoint existing files.
- New files may be created freely, but each name must be unique to its package.
- Some packages add optional fields or parameters only so that a package in the next wave can compile. Each one is marked "contract for wave N". Add them exactly as written, even if nothing in your package uses them.

Translations (i18n)
- Put new keys in src/i18n/ext/<package-id>.ts and export {de, en, tr}. The aggregator in src/i18n/index.ts merges every ext file after the base dictionaries.
- All three languages must have the same keys and the same placeholders. tests/i18n.test.ts checks this.
- To change the wording of an existing key, override it in your own ext file. First grep src/i18n/ext to make sure no other ext file already overrides that key.
- Never edit de.ts, en.ts or tr.ts.

CSS
- Only w2-design-system edits src/ui/styles.css.
- Every other package puts its CSS in src/ui/css/<package-id>.css and imports it from a component it owns.

Tests
- Unit tests go in tests/<package-id>*.test.ts.
- Browser checks are standalone Playwright scripts at e2e/<package-id>.e2e.cjs, run against `npm run preview`.
- Only w7-docs-e2e touches e2e/run-e2e.cjs and README.md.
- The golden mosaic hash fixture is tests/golden/mosaic-hashes.json. It hashes kind, c1, c2, rec, sub, line, free and palette hex+code, but not names. It is owned by whichever package owns src/core/mosaic.ts in that wave. Any change to it must be deliberate and explained in the PR.

Quality bar
- Every package must leave `npm run typecheck`, `npm test`, `npm run build` and the existing `node e2e/run-e2e.cjs` green.
- Every package must keep the exact-geometry and count guarantees: totals equal the geometry, and cut dimensions come only from analyzeCut on real polygons.
- Anything estimated must be labelled 'Schätzung' or 'Richtwert'. Requirement 18 holds everywhere.
deferred: Grout compensation in computeMosaic (algo-quality#0, part 4). Both reviewers called it optional and off by default, and recommending a grout plus an honest preview gives most of the benefit. Changing the factory grout default from #BDB8AE to #808080 is deferred too; the recommendation never overwrites the user's choice.

Linear-light averaging of stone target colours (algo-quality#10). Measured gains are within k-means noise on natural photos. Revisit it together with linear-light resizing in imageOps, with a measured A/B benchmark.

Mixed tile sizes stage 2: zones with their own grid (spec-gaps#2). Wave 6 delivers stage 1, real fine-tile materials for k×k sub-stones plus fine regions. Zones touch every per-cell structure (progress mask, IDs, sections, hit-testing, PDF), and the tiles-step badge stays honest until then.

Movable section boundaries and a seam optimiser (spec-gaps#9). This is impact 2-3 and needs new settings across layout, viewer, worker and PDF. Paper-matched section presets (wave 6) cover the main paper-waste pain.
Full SVG export of plans and templates (spec-gaps#12). The vector PDF at 1:1 or custom paper already covers plotters. Only PNG preview export is built (wave 6).

Diff-based incremental statistics in a worker that keeps its own mosaic copy, and dirty-pixel overview updates (performance-scale#5, parts 2-3). They are replaced by the 8-13x single-pass stats (wave 5), coalesced stats jobs and O(1) progress counters (wave 4). Revisit only if 5M-stone edits are still slower than about 1 s.
Splitting the shape analysis across several workers (performance-scale#7, part b). The hot-loop fix gives about 4x. SharedArrayBuffer is not available without COOP/COEP headers.
One CSV per section, delivered as a ZIP (performance-scale#1). Streaming CSV plus the Excel row-limit warning are built; a store-only ZIP can follow if users ask.
Automatic stock-constrained recolouring (spec-gaps#4, part 4). It would change how the image looks and is often impossible. Exact shortfall and shopping lists are built instead.

Error-driven k-means swap refinement and detail-weighted palette samples (algo-quality#6, optional part). Measured gains were inconsistent. Pinned accent colours confirmed by the user are built instead.
Dither error diffusion through split/SUB cells, serpentine scanning and face/edge damping (algo-quality#1). Measured as useless or harmful.
Global cut budget, 'max. Schnittzellen' (algo-quality#3, phase 2). The background cut factor in wave 4 gives most of the value.
Image-level Canny/polyline contour extraction (algo-quality#5). Unproven, and it would defeat template reuse. Only the opt-in grid-preserving continuity bonus is built.
Haptic feedback with the VIBRATE permission (ux-mobile-android#2). The text status line and flash highlight already give feedback.
A native 'pause' flush registry through @capacitor/app (ux-mobile-android#1). beforeunload with commit(), visibilitychange and minimizeApp already cover saving.
MediaPipe face detection. Its 14.6 MB wasm exceeds the PWA precache limit; pico.js is used instead (wave 4).
Colour-chart sheet mode for measuring many tiles from one photo (spec-gaps#7, phase 2).
First-fit-decreasing packing of mixed-width strips into shared raw tiles (correctness-core#5, optional). The current per-shape-group count is a safe upper bound.
Mixed page orientations per section and tighter print margins (pdf-print#4). Mixed orientations risk print-dialog auto-scaling, which breaks 1:1. Smaller margins clip on common printers.
Undo history that persists across reloads (ux-desktop#7). The journal is in memory for the session only, and the README will say so.
